name: Card stack
one_line: Many variants of one object fanned or stacked in overlap, so range reads at a glance
summary: Copies of one kind of object, each a different variant, overlap in a pile or fan that deals out, shuffles or spreads. Range reads at once, where a slideshow makes the viewer wait for it. It suits showing a collection or choice. A lead card steadies it; every card moving at once reads as noise, and mismatched cards undercut the set.

routes.one_line: Cards as vector groups, dealt and fanned on a seekable timeline in the browser

steps.does: Author each card as a vector group with a shared frame and its own variant
Deal, rotate and spread the cards with offset onsets, seeked per frame

limits: Suits drawn vectors; supplied stills would be embedded as image elements, which no evidence covers
WAAPI evidence is transform, stroke draw and stagger on Chromium; stacking order changes are untested
SVG evidence is one static raster by resvg; no browser rendering of a card set was exercised

routes.one_line: Supplied stills as GPU sprites in a pile, dealt and shuffled from t

steps.does: Draw each still as a card with its own transform and draw order, set from t

limits: Suits supplied raster stills; PixiJS evidence is Graphics geometry only, not sprites or textures
Rounded corners and card shadows are untested; they may need masks or filters
Draw-order shuffles need a per-frame ordering you must write; none is evidenced

routes.one_line: Cards as planes in a Three.js scene, so the fan can turn with real depth and a camera

steps.does: Place card planes with textures in depth and drive their poses from t

limits: Suits supplied stills as textures or drawn vectors rasterised first; neither is in the evidence
Evidence is one render-per-seek scene on a stand-in browser; card textures and shadows are untested
Heavier than a flat route; use it only when the fan needs perspective

source: references/motion-director §4.1, §4.2; references/image-direction §5.1; tool records as of 2026-11-20
